summary: preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook that runs setup.mjs, which downloads a Bun runtime binary from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, chmod +x's it, and uses it to execFileSync a sibling file math_init.js bundled as a Bun-compiled module (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`). Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are obfuscator.io-style opaque code (hex-identifier renaming, string-array rotation decoders), so the payload cannot be inspected or run under Node. A React table component has no functional reason to require a second language runtime or to execute an obfuscated bundle at install time. Provenance is also inconsistent: package.json homepage points to github.com/qlik-oss/sprout while CHANGELOG.md references github.com/qlik-trial/sprout-react-table, and the public repo does not advertise a Bun-executed install-time payload. The result is full-host code execution under the installer's account on every `npm install`, driven by opaque bytes delivered through an alternate runtime specifically chosen to defeat Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
